title: Why Tarragona tastes the way it does

lede.text: A coastal plain and an inland river valley share one denomination, and their wines are clearly different. Near the sea the whites are soft and aromatic; inland, where water is scarcer, the grapes are rich in sugar and suit liqueur wines.

chapters.title: A coast and a river
paras: The denomination covers the Catalan vineyards of the Camp de Tarragona districts and part of the Ribera d'Ebre district. One municipality, Masllorenç, belongs to the Baix Penedès.

The coastal area is flat to gently rolling and open to the sea. It runs from the coast north to Valls and west to the fertile land around Reus and Mont-roig del Camp. Joan Miró painted it in 1919-22, inspired by his family's house in Mont-roig del Camp.

The other area is the Ribera d'Ebre. Vines grow in the valley between Vinebre and the Sierra de Cardó, on limy, stony slopes or on alluvial land beside the river. That river carries more water than any other in the Iberian Peninsula.

fly.label: Mont-roig del Camp, Miró's plain
fly.caption: The open plain near Mont-roig del Camp that Joan Miró painted in 1919-22.

fly.label: Vinebre, the Ebro valley
fly.caption: Vines grow in the Ribera d'Ebre valley, between Vinebre and the Sierra de Cardó, on stony slopes or on alluvial land beside the river.

chapters.title: A mountain range splits the weather
paras: The Cordillera Prelitoral, the range just inland of the coast, hinders any uniform climate and creates many microclimates. The main split is between a coastal sector under maritime influence and an inland sector under continental influence.
The whole Camp de Tarragona has a Mediterranean climate. Even so, the weather does not behave exactly the same everywhere: the relief and the distance from the sea, among other things, shape it.
On the northern and western side of the range, continental air currents make temperatures more extreme.

chapters.title: Poor, limy ground
paras: In the Camp de Tarragona many vineyard soils have low fertility, limited by low phosphorus. Potassium levels are good, as in most vineyard soils, and this favours the metabolism of sugars and so the alcohol level.
Clay parent material comes with a limy crust. That crust stops planting in the areas most exposed to erosion, so vines sit in the hollows, which gather soil washed in from the sides.

In the Ribera d'Ebre the vines grow on terraces. The soils come from limy materials, clays and marls among them. Water shortage is greater here, which is likely why the harvest per hectare is smaller and the alcohol higher inland.

Across the denomination, active lime runs from 2.5% to 27.75% and the pH from 7.11 to 8.63, so the soils are slightly alkaline. Organic matter is relatively low, at 0.7% to 1.3%, and loam is the main texture.

fly.label: Sierra de Tivissa
fly.caption: The slopes of the Sierra de Tivissa shed glacis, gentle sloping fans, that run mainly east to west.

chapters.title: From soft whites to liqueur wines
paras: Tarragona makes white, rosado (rosé) and red wine. It also makes brisado, a wine from white grapes fermented on their skins, and quality sparkling wine. Needle wine, a lightly fizzy style, and the liqueur wines complete the range.

White grapes include Macabeo and Xarel·lo. Red grapes include Garnacha and Samsó, also called Cariñena. In the Ribera d'Ebre the reds join the body and colour of Cariñena with the richness of Garnacha.

Near the sea the whites are very soft, balanced and aromatic. That holds for the dry whites and for the sparkling and needle ones. The reds are firm and aromatic. The rosados are a very bright cherry colour. In the Ribera d'Ebre the whites are bright.

Inland grapes especially suit the liqueur wines. There the soil and the climate, where water shortage is most evident, give grapes high in sugar. Mistela is made by adding wine alcohol to must, and it ends with more than 100 g/l of sugar. Moscatel is made from Moscatel de Alejandría and Moscatel Frontignan. Rancio ages in contact with air, and its characteristic colour is old gold. These three finish between 15% and 22% alcohol.

Garnacha liqueur wine is made from Garnacha Negra and Garnacha Blanca. It and Clásico also finish between 15% and 22%. Clásico has more than 50 g/l of residual sugar. Vino de Misa, the altar wine, finishes at 15% to 20%. The liqueur wines are fortified: wine alcohol is added, though Rancio takes it only if needed and Garnacha may take mistela instead.
Vimblanc is a sweet wine from grapes dried in the sun and night air on tables. No alcohol is added. The sugar is so concentrated that the yeasts stop fermenting early.

Sparkling wine is made two ways. The traditional method ferments a second time in the bottle and spends at least nine months in the cellar. The ancestral method finishes its one fermentation in the bottle, and the pink version uses Trepat.

terms.text: A red has 2 years of ageing in total, with at least 6 months in oak barrels of up to 330 l. A white or rosado has 18 months, with at least 6 in such barrels.

A red has at least 3 years of ageing, with at least 12 months in oak barrels of up to 330 l and the rest in bottle. A white or rosado has at least 2 years, with at least 6 months in such barrels. On a quality sparkling wine it means at least 15 months from bottling to disgorging.
A red has at least 5 years of ageing, with at least 24 months in oak barrels of up to 330 l and the rest in bottle. A white or rosado has at least 4 years, with at least 6 months in such barrels.
A young wine. It is sold only with the harvest year on the label and is bottled within that year's campaign or from a date set by the harvest, the winemaking and the quality.
Barrel-fermented: the wine fermented in wooden vessels of up to 600 l.
Barrel: the wine's information gives the time in months and years and the type of wooden vessel, of up to 600 l.
Oak: the wine's information gives the time in months or years spent in oak vessels of up to 600 l.
A wine for keeping: at least 12 months in oak, then bottled and sold.
